turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Nuala Brennan? Come on in and we'll do the blood pressure before the doctor.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Lovely. Arm out for me. Any pain in the arm?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): That's one fifty-two over eighty-eight, and the pulse is seventy-four. A bit high. I'll stick it on the screen.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was half running in from the car park, so she was.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Sure that wouldn't help it. Doctor O'Shea is just caught with the computer. He'll be in.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry about that. The yoke logged me out again. Mrs Brennan, routine review, is it?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Um, one second, it's loading. Right so. The high blood pressure and the cholesterol. How are you keeping?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Are you taking the tablets?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Some.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Some? Say that again, I clicked the wrong bit.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Some.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's after stopping the cholesterol tablet. She still has the blood pressure one.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): You've stopped the cholesterol one, the atorvastatin twenty milligrams at night. Is that it?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did you stop it?
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was reading this thing online, your man going on about statins and the liver and—
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Months.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Months, is it. Can you get nearer than that, before Christmas or after?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Dunno.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): January, I'd say. Don't write that in stone, she hasn't a clue.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the date open so. What had you worried in the article?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Online.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): I heard online. Was there a particular bit?
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Muscles, the liver, and that you'd be better off the statin. I told her ring the surgery, but she had them binned.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to give out. Half the internet is at that. Any muscle pain on you?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sometimes? Sorry, again, the screen hopped.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nothing definite, so. The ramipril for the blood pressure, are you still taking that?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Every morning?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not every morning. I missed it with the login. How are you taking it?
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Every other day. She's still on the ramipril for the blood pressure, and the box says five milligrams.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Five milligrams on the box. Nuala, what do you think the dose is?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ten? Say it once more, please.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She might be mixing the boxes. I have the diabetes myself. Metformin, five hundred milligrams, morning and night. Those are mine, not hers.

[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hold on. The metformin is your husband's, Tom, not yours. I'm not putting that on your list, Nuala. And I still can't tell if the ramipril is five or ten, so the dose stays blank till I see the box.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): His.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): His, yes. Any chest pain, Nuala?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Shortness of breath?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): What did they say about the last blood test, do you remember?
[SEG0051] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They told her the cholesterol was—
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Borderline.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Borderline. That was the cholesterol result?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0055] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The cholesterol test from before she stopped. They said it was borderline. No actual number.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): No number, then I won't invent one. The old report isn't up on this thing anyway. Any allergies to tablets?
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke at all?
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0060] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She gave the cigarettes up years ago.
[SEG0061] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. Let me listen in. Deep breath... Chest is clear, and no swelling around the ankles.
[SEG0062] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's something, anyway.
[SEG0063] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, it froze on me again. Well, actually, I'm not starting the atorvastatin back today.
[SEG0064] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Would she not be safer back on it?
[SEG0065] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll see the numbers before we decide. I'm sending her for repeat bloods, the cholesterol, the liver, and the kidney function, with her being on the ramipril.
[SEG0066] person_1 (NURSE): I can take those bloods outside once you're finished, if you want them today.
[SEG0067] person_4 (DOCTOR): Today is perfect. Nuala, try and take the ramipril every morning now, not every second day.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): Right.
[SEG0069] person_4 (DOCTOR): And don't be stopping tablets over something you read online without a word to us.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): Aye.
[SEG0071] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bring the ramipril box in next time so we can settle the dose.
[SEG0072] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll put his metformin in a different press, so the boxes aren't together.
[SEG0073] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do that at home, yes. We'll look at the statin decision again in a month, when those bloods are back.
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand.
[SEG0075] person_4 (DOCTOR): If you get a pain in the chest, ring the surgery the same day. Don't sit on it.
[SEG0076] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A month's time, and the bloods today. Grand.
[SEG0077] person_1 (NURSE): Cholesterol, liver, and the kidneys. I'll call her in a minute.
[SEG0078] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's them. Thanks, Siobhan.
[SEG0079] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Come on, Nuala.
[SEG0080] person_2 (PATIENT): Right.

spec.situation: Patient on routine review who admits stopping the cholesterol tablet after reading something online, still takes the BP tablet but 'every other day'; mentions husband's diabetes pills; doctor does not scold, plans repeat blood tests and revisits the statin decision in a month.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Diabetes mentioned as family member's own condition, not family history of patient.
Family member, not husband, reported 5 mg; doctor left dose blank due discrepancy.
bad.text: The husband said the ramipril box is five milligrams but the patient said the dose is ten, and the dose was left blank. (type=medication_discrepancy, related_entities=medications[1], resolution_status=unresolved)

omissions.text: Ramipril dose was explicitly left unresolved/blank because the doctor could not confirm whether it was 5 mg or 10 mg until seeing the box; the recorded medication entry for ramipril omits the unknown dose status.
Doctor decided not to restart atorvastatin at this visit pending blood results ('I'm not starting the atorvastatin back today').
Repeat blood tests were intended to be done today if possible, and nurse offered to take them today; doctor agreed 'Today is perfect.'
Follow-up plan was specifically to review the statin decision again in a month when the bloods are back, not just a generic follow-up consultation.

Patient reported she is not taking ramipril every morning; current use is every other day. This nonadherence detail is present, but the explicit denial of daily morning dosing was also stated by the patient.

Former smoking history was confirmed by patient as current non-smoker and by family member as quit years ago; only the family member statement is captured, not the patient's direct denial of current smoking.
